decisions.summary: Skeleton with documented contracts, not implementations
decisions.rationale: Chris fills in implementations and I review; under DADP the docstring is what Codex tests against, so contracts first makes validation meaningful.
decisions.tradeoff: Nothing runs end-to-end. Mitigated by py_compile on all 13 modules.
decisions.test_implication: Test only build_targets(), config shape, and import integrity. Do not write behavioural tests for NotImplementedError bodies.

decisions.summary: Enum and range constraints enforced in the database, not just Pydantic
decisions.rationale: Pydantic validates model output; it does not cover migrations, repair scripts, or a psql prompt. If a fact must be true of the data rather than of one code path, it belongs in the schema.
decisions.tradeoff: Changing an enum now needs a migration.
decisions.test_implication: Test with RAW SQL bypassing the ORM. An ORM-level test proves nothing about a DB constraint. Blocked on OQ-1 + OQ-2.

decisions.summary: embedding_dim=0 sentinel raises at import of db/models.py
decisions.rationale: The dangerous failure is not forgetting OQ-1, it is guessing a plausible 1024 and discovering three weeks of embeddings are garbage. A value that cannot work turns silent misconfiguration into a self-explaining crash.
decisions.tradeoff: Nothing importing models.py runs until OQ-1 is answered, including tests.
decisions.test_implication: Assert the RuntimeError fires and names OQ-1 when embedding_dim <= 0.

decisions.summary: NEAREST_CENTROID_SQL as a named module constant with a consequence comment
decisions.rationale: INV-2 is one WHERE clause, its violation is invisible downstream, and the resulting bad cluster outranks correct ones because distinct_authors is the sum of both industries. Inlined, it looks like a convenience filter someone can tidy away.
decisions.tradeoff: Raw SQL rather than ORM; needed anyway for the <=> operator.
decisions.test_implication: Cycle 2, once assignment is implemented: the two-part partition test from .spec/modules/cluster.md.

decisions.summary: Pure/impure split - classify() and compute_score() take primitives
decisions.rationale: Otherwise every filter rule and scoring weight is only reachable through a database, and those tests get written thinly or not at all.
decisions.tradeoff: Two functions per stage instead of one.
decisions.test_implication: SPEC_DEVIATION - both module specs marked this INFERRED. Probe that the split exists and the pure functions are DB-free.

decisions.summary: PAIN_PATTERNS and scoring weights live in config.py
decisions.rationale: They are the same kind of thing as VERTICALS keywords - tuning knobs edited while watching the pass rate. One file to open when tuning.
decisions.tradeoff: config.py holds regexes, which is mildly odd.
decisions.test_implication: Every PAIN_PATTERNS entry compiles; each is checked against a pathological input under a timeout.

decisions.summary: Added pyproject.toml with runtime dependencies only, no test deps
decisions.rationale: dadp.md's no-dependencies rule governs protocol adoption, not building. Test deps are excluded because the Validator owns the framework choice and only the Builder may edit the manifest.
decisions.tradeoff: Codex cannot install its own test framework; must file a blocker.
decisions.test_implication: OQ-9 - file a BLOCKER naming the exact test deps rather than editing pyproject.toml.

migrations/ and alembic.ini deliberately NOT written - blocked on OQ-1, a migration against a guessed vector(N) would be thrown away
test_targets: build_targets() - every VERTICALS subreddit with correct hint, every SHARED_SUBREDDITS entry with None, no duplicates
config shape - exactly 2 verticals, all 3 keys each, non-empty; ENRICHMENT_VERTICALS == VERTICAL_NAMES + ('neither',)
PAIN_PATTERNS - all compile; robustness against pathological input under a timeout

Schema constraints via RAW SQL: dup (source, external_id); dup raw_post_id; out-of-enum vertical; relevance=11; vertical='neither' with relevance=3; distinct_authors > member_count [BLOCKED on OQ-1, OQ-2]
SPEC_DEVIATION probes: distinct_authors CHECK constraint, pure/impure split
config.py is the sole os.environ reader - greppable assertion over the package
No hardcoded vertical literal in a conditional outside config.py - greppable assertion
Import integrity - every entry in WorkerSettings.functions and cron_jobs resolves to a real callable [BLOCKED on OQ-1]
known_edge_cases: db/models.py raises RuntimeError on import while settings.embedding_dim <= 0 (OQ-1). Test targets 4 and 8 are blocked behind it; 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 are runnable today.
Every pipeline function raises NotImplementedError. Behavioural tests against them are not meaningful this cycle.
No migration exists, so there is no schema to run DB tests against.

findings.detail: build_targets emits every configured target with the correct hint and no duplicates.
Config shape, enrichment vertical derivation, regex compilation, and hostile-input timeout checks pass.
The pure functions are synchronous, primitive-argument, and DB-free; outer stage functions are coroutines.
Declared unique and distinct-author constraints exist in SQLAlchemy metadata, and the OQ-1 import tripwire fires.
Python files compile; environment and vertical-branch boundaries hold; worker callables and cron targets resolve under test stubs; nearest-centroid SQL keeps its vertical clause.
Seven registered ARQ functions omit ctx; six will raise TypeError and embed_pending will receive the context dict as batch_size.
Enrichment accepts vertical='neither' with nonzero relevance despite the declared invariant.
Raw-SQL schema tests and the two-part semantic INV-2 partition test cannot run without the resolved vector dimension, migration, and real pgvector database.
pytest and pytest-asyncio exist locally but are not declared, so a clean checkout cannot reproduce validation.

findings.target: manual LLM and digest acceptance criteria
findings.detail: Pain-point phrasing, vertical disagreements, and digest usefulness still require a human validation path.
The directory is still not a Git repository, so DADP has no version-control audit trail.

open_blockers.detail: Voyage embedding model ID and its vector dimension are unset. The initial Alembic migration cannot declare vector(N) without them, and changing N later requires re-embedding every row. Blocks the migration, real db.models import, DB integration tests, and all of chunk 3. Cycle 1 isolated structural tests use a test-only positive dimension and Vector stub.

No local Postgres+pgvector or Redis is defined. The file would be consumed by source at runtime and by tests as a fixture, so ownership under the DADP write boundary is ambiguous. Builder-owned by the letter of the rule, but the Validator cannot run an integration test without it.

Undecided whether integration tests against live Postgres+pgvector are in scope. INV-2 (cluster vertical partition) and INV-7 (distinct-author counting) are SQL-level invariants that a mocked DB cannot meaningfully test.

A large share of the human's acceptance criteria in specs/ are deliberately manual judgement calls about LLM output quality (eyeball 20 pain_points, read the digest as its recipient, hand-check vertical disagreements). They are real requirements with no assertion form. Unresolved how they enter the DADP loop.
Repo is not under version control. DADP's audit trail assumes history exists. Recommend git init before further build cycles.

Test dependencies are absent by design (DECISION-1.7). pyproject.toml is Builder-owned. Codex must file a blocker naming the exact test deps (recommended: pytest, pytest-asyncio) rather than editing the manifest.
Seven registered ARQ functions omit the required ctx-first job signature. Add ctx to the stage contracts or register Builder-owned ctx wrappers.
Enrichment accepts vertical='neither' with nonzero relevance. Add cross-field validation so invalid model output is rejected before the DB insert.
